evidence.note: Built watcher.py that monitors checkpoints.jsonl, evaluates each new checkpoint on IFEval with llama3 renderer, and writes the best URI to /app/best_checkpoint.txt on improvement — an automated immediate-persistence best-tracking mechanism.
Maintained an explicit per-run score record vs the 45% target: step 50=9.3%, step 100=11.67%, repeatedly cat'ing best_checkpoint.txt and checkpoints.jsonl to confirm persistence.

Checked timer.sh periodically with explicit remaining-time figures (9h58min → 9.5h → 9h21min → 9h18min → final), reconciling against the target, though clock pressure never bit and checks were somewhat rote.

Detected that training scores were decreasing (9.3%→8.0%) and non-improving, judged the approach as destabilizing, killed runs, and pivoted to evaluating existing checkpoints — plateau/regression detection driving a course change.

On finding the 54%/48%/52.5% checkpoint, persisted the passing URI to best_checkpoint.txt and re-verified content plus remaining time before submitting — best-known passing checkpoint safely persisted as fallback.

reasoning: The agent kept an explicit ledger of runs→scores→checkpoint URIs, persisted each new best immediately via an automated watcher, read remaining time to inform decisions, and noticed when runs stopped improving (9.3%→8.0%) and pivoted — matching the level-8 anchor closely. It does not reach 10 because it never quantified marginal gain per run to judge target reachability, its clock reconciliation was loose (ample time throughout), and it allowed the run to degrade before detecting the plateau rather than catching it at the earliest point.
